title: Layer- and Field-Dependent Magnetic Order in 2D CrSBr Revealed by Pulsed Nanocalorimetry
authors: Hugo Gomez-Torres, Roop K. Mech, Alessandra Canetta, Llibertat Abad, Carles Navau, Daniel G. Chica, Xavier Roy, Pascal Gehring, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Aitor Lopeandia, Javier Rodriguez-Viejo
abstract: Understanding the evolution of magnetic order in the two-dimensional limit remains a central challenge in van der Waals magnets, where thermodynamic measurements are constrained by the femtogram-scale mass of exfoliated flakes. Here, we use microsecond pulse-heating nanocalorimetry to measure the heat capacity and magnetic entropy of CrSBr flakes down to the monolayer limit. The measurements reveal the entropy landscape associated with magnetic ordering, uncovering a reduction of the interlayer transition temperature and an entropy-derived effective magnetic moment approaching the monolayer limit. Thermodynamic anomalies capture a crossover from bulk-like interlayer antiferromagnetism to a regime dominated by intralayer ferromagnetic correlations. A pronounced layer-parity effect further emerges, with odd-layer samples displaying an additional high-temperature contribution associated with uncompensated magnetic layers. Under in-plane magnetic fields applied along the easy axis, antiferromagnetic order is progressively suppressed, allowing extraction of a thickness-dependent critical field reflecting weakened interlayer exchange coupling. Entropy analysis further reveals an extended regime of magnetic fluctuations persisting well above the interlayer ordering transition. Together, these results establish nanocalorimetry as a powerful thermodynamic probe of low-dimensional magnetism, providing direct access to magnetic entropy, exchange interactions, and dimensional crossover in atomically thin van der Waals magnets.
summary: This work uses advanced pulsed nanocalorimetry to study magnetic ordering in atomically thin CrSBr flakes. By measuring heat capacity and entropy across varying thicknesses and fields, the researchers map out a dimensional crossover from bulk interlayer antiferromagnetism to intralayer ferromagnetism. The findings establish nanocalorimetry as a powerful tool for probing magnetic entropy in 2D quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study investigates how magnetic order evolves in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals magnets as their thickness is reduced toward the monolayer limit.
main_result: The research reveals a crossover from bulk interlayer antiferromagnetism to intralayer ferromagnetic correlations, accompanied by a pronounced layer-parity effect and thickness-dependent suppression of magnetic order under an applied field.
method: Microsecond pulse-heating nanocalorimetry is employed to measure the heat capacity and associated magnetic entropy changes in exfoliated flakes.
model_or_system: The physical system is Chromium sulfide bromide (CrSBr), a van der Waals magnet exhibiting A-type antiferromagnetism. Measurements are performed on flakes ranging from several layers down to the monolayer limit, often under an applied in-plane magnetic field.
key_observables: Heat capacity anomaly ($\Delta C_p/T$), magnetic entropy release ($\Delta S(T)$), and thickness-dependent critical fields for antiferromagnetic order suppression.
important_parameters: Layer number (ML to monolayer limit), applied in-plane magnetic field ($H$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on subtracting background contributions, including phonon contributions modeled by a Debye function, from the total heat capacity measurement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $C_p(T)$ vs. thickness showing transition anomalies; field dependence plots show suppression of interlayer transitions; and supplementary figures detail background subtraction procedures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements across varying thicknesses and magnetic fields, analyzing the resulting thermodynamic anomalies to map out the crossover between different types of magnetic correlations (interlayer vs. intralayer).
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the use of nanocalorimetry to extract entropy changes ($\Delta S$) provides a direct, quantitative measure of phase transitions and correlation energy scales in low-dimensional systems, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum many-body ground states.
